verdict: supports narrow provisional source-description finding; minor; direction null
checks: Read SDC’s complete first page and immediately following requests; read the JIM 2025 introduction, methods, Internet-and-Smartphone section, and German/English summaries.
Independently retrieved the original publisher PDF through web; visually inspected SDC physical PDF page 1 and JIM physical PDF page 27 / printed page 25.
source_definition: The JIM 231-minute measure is daily smartphone screen time among 960 owners able to read their device display. The report expressly replaces its previous unspecific online-time reporting with this measure. It does not report 231 minutes of all-device internet use for all 1,200 respondents.
context_challenge: Smartphones are a major route to online services and many listed apps need connectivity; colloquial shorthand could explain the wording. Nonetheless smartphone screen time and online duration across devices are different measured variables.
limits: This establishes incorrect description of the cited measurement, not a different actual online-time estimate. Screen time can include offline use and online use can occur on other devices. No net numerical inflation/deflation is established.
severity_and_direction: Minor: introductory background loses measurement and denominator qualifications; the argument for child protection remains. Null direction is appropriate because neither true all-device duration nor its difference from 231 minutes is established.

evidence.title: JIM 2025
evidence.locator: Physical PDF page 5 / printed page 3; physical PDF page 27 / printed page 25, chart and surrounding prose; German/English summaries.

suggested_limit: Avoid saying 231 minutes is false as the true online duration or that it strengthens the request. Keep the mismatch in the source label and population.
